derived_results.claim: For p_rho=Ae^{-bW}+Ce^{-cW}, p_theta=Be^{-aW}, a=lambda b+(1-lambda)c, weighted AM-GM cancels the common W exponent and gives a closed upper envelope B lambda^lambda(1-lambda)^(1-lambda)/(A^lambda C^(1-lambda)) for every W>=0.

The log AM-GM envelope is strictly increasing in |y| over the relevant symmetric domain after maximizing candidate mean at clip(y,[-h,h]). If any theta has negative H_mu then |y|<=h+u/sqrt(m), so the entire negative-curvature use case reduces to the single boundary y*=h+u/sqrt(m), independent of sigma.

A 20,000-box mpmath.iv enclosure over sigma in [ell+1e-8,u-1e-8], plus conservative endpoint strips, gives ratio upper 3.8163015958; rounding to 3.817 replaces the old 461.24628 negative-branch ratio envelope for the fixed-rho r90 setup.

Using ratio<=3.817 with old H_lower=-36.63619705 yields L>=-139.840364 instead of -16898.309604. On the prior 300k-sample worst cell, the same Maurer-Pontil radius falls from 3.23242344 to 0.61852466 and the lower confidence margin rises from 13.59358845 to 16.20748723.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The analytic AM-GM and y-monotonicity reductions are exact, but the final sigma enclosure is only certified within the mpmath.iv backend; no separate MPFI/Arb-style directed-rounding reproduction was performed this run.
rho remains the fixed point 0.55441744 rather than a certified rho interval.
The 3.817 bound is scoped to y values for which some null theta can have H_mu<0, which is exactly the negative branch used by r90; arbitrary-y pointwise ratio is not claimed.

The improved empirical-Bernstein margin reuses r90 sample mean/variance and is therefore a deterministic consequence of the new range bound plus the prior randomized sample, not a fresh randomized validation stream.

candidate_new.mechanism: Use natural-precision interpolation plus weighted AM-GM to eliminate sufficient-statistic W exactly, prove monotonicity in y, and leave only a one-dimensional sigma interval enclosure. This converts the former huge global ratio range into a near-tight constant for negative-curvature cells.
candidate_new.status: exact reduction + backend interval enclosure; independent directed-rounding reproduction and rho-interval transport pending

frontier: Recompute the full 256-cell r90 randomized screen with the 3.817 range premise to expose true worst cells and choose the smallest deterministic quadrature target set.
Outward-integrate the exact L_cell envelope deterministically on those worst cells, now that the negative tail range is only about [-140,100] instead of [-16898,100].
Reproduce the one-dimensional sigma bound with an independent interval backend and extend across a certified rho interval.
Complete r89 C_tt with outward-rounded transcendentals; then solve rho and four active-corner directional expectations under directed rounding.
exact_next_action: Apply ratio<=3.817 to the saved r90 pointwise-envelope sampler statistics and, if reproducible state is available, rerun the 256-cell independent validation to identify the true minimum-margin cell under the tightened bounded range. Then perform outward-rounded deterministic quadrature of L_cell on that cell set. In parallel port the 1D sigma enclosure to a second interval implementation and rho interval.
